edu-2012-001.note: NCES 2010-040 p.3: 72% of teachers used LCD/DLP projectors sometimes or often for instruction in 2009; well over 5% at placement.

edu-2012-002.note: Cooney Center Level Up Learning (2014): 74% of K-8 teachers use digital games for instruction; over 5% by 2014.

edu-2012-003.note: NCES 2010-040: 57% of teachers used interactive whiteboards sometimes or often in 2009; over 5% at placement.

edu-2012-004.note: ClassDojo (EdSurge 2014-03-12) awards behaviour points and avoids badges, so it does not support the claim; hit holds on Khan Academy badges (about 10M monthly users Feb 2014, ~65% US, SRI 2014 brief), over 5% of US K-12 students.

edu-2012-005.note: TechCrunch 2013-03-06: Edmodo at 18M users, mostly US K-12; far above 5% of US teachers/students by 2014. Grader A's Wikipedia counts not found on the page.

edu-2012-006.note: Speak Up 2013 (Flipped Learning Network PDF): 46% of teachers use online videos in instruction, 16% regularly create video lessons.

edu-2012-008.note: Babson 'Opening the Curriculum' 2014 (ED572730): ~34% of faculty aware of OER and 79% of those use it, so >5% of faculty used open materials by 2014. Grader B misquotes Babson 2013 (ED541571 says 2.6% offer a MOOC, 9.4% planning, not 5.0%/9.3%).

edu-2012-010.note: Gallup/Google 2016: 25% (2015) and 40% (2016) of US K-12 principals report CS classes with programming; Hour of Code 2013 used Scratch/Blockly at scale. Over 5% by 2014.

edu-2012-011.note: SLJ surveys: 54% of US school libraries offered ebooks in 2013, 66% in 2014 (via search; SLJ page blocked to fetch). Over 5% by 2015.

edu-2012-012.note: TechCrunch 2013-02-28: 4.5M iPads sold to US educational institutions by Feb 2013, over 5% of ~50M US K-12 students before Y=2014.

edu-2012-013.note: Gallup 2016 table: 40% of US K-12 schools offer 'programming or coding to create things such as websites, apps or video games' (25% in 2015); over 5% by 2017.

edu-2012-014.note: Krutka/Carpenter 2014: ~30% of a self-selected Twitter-using educator sample backchannel, mostly at conferences; real but no evidence of 5% of classes. Partial.

edu-2012-015.note: TechCrunch 2012: Parchment e-transcripts used by more than 30% of US high schools plus 1,800 universities; digital records exchange over 5% before Y=2016.

edu-2012-016.note: Quest to Learn described as one of two game-design-based US public schools; Cooney 2014 shows classroom games mostly pre-made. Real niche use, partial.

edu-2012-017.note: NCES 2012-008: 55% of US districts had students in distance-education courses in 2009-10 (1,816,400 enrollments), many delivered by other districts or state virtual schools. Hit, earlier counts.

edu-2012-018.note: NWEA MAP Growth (5.2M students fall 2019) gives teachers growth reports; hit holds on that. Grader B misreads Gallup/NewSchools 2019: 35% cite actionable data as a selection criterion, not 50% saying tools provide it.

edu-2012-019.note: EdWeek Research Center 2019: 60% of educators never/rarely use adaptive software for own-pace learning, so ~40% do at least sometimes; over 5% by 2019.

edu-2012-020.note: Speak Up 2013: 16% of math and science teachers implement flipped learning with video; over 5% of teachers well before 2019.

edu-2012-021.note: No measure of school share: 3ders/Y Soft 2017 says 23% of vendor-survey respondents use 3D printing at primary level (not 23% of K-12 schools, as grader B reads it); MakerBot's 7,000 classroom printers (Voxelmatters 2019) is ~5% of US schools only if one per school. Evidence cannot separate hit from partial.

edu-2012-022.note: NWEA: 5.2M students took computer-adaptive MAP Growth in fall 2019; NPR 2018: Utah and Ohio machine-score state test essays. Over 5% by 2021.

edu-2012-023.note: ALEKS (Wikipedia) uses knowledge-space maps but shows students a pie, not a navigable map; Khan Academy's student-facing knowledge map was retired. Real but limited use of the visual map, partial.

edu-2012-024.note: SMART Table classroom use documented in small studies (IGI 2019, ERIC EJ1102740) and reseller listings; no evidence of 5% of classrooms. Partial.

edu-2012-027.note: Brainly peer-to-peer homework network reached 200M monthly users in March 2020 (Brainly release, via search; page 403s to fetch), over 5% of school-age students in its markets before 2024.

edu-2012-028.note: Interactive walls and CAVE rooms exist in some schools and universities (Neoxperiences ~500 installs, Wikipedia CAVE); classrooms use front-of-room panels. Real use below 5% by 2026, partial.

edu-2012-029.note: EDUCAUSE 2023: 91% of surveyed higher-ed students used Canvas Mobile in 2021, 66% use a mobile learning app weekly; Duolingo mass-market. Over 5% before 2026.
